column1: # Move explanations: key (position before the move | uci), then the text. Written from flagged moves.

column2:
You asked why not take. There are two takes, so here is each.
Why Black does not take on e4 first: 12...dxe4 13.Nxe4 hits the bishop on c5, which has to retreat (13...Ba7). The engine puts that at about a third of a pawn for White, and it gives up the d5 pawn that holds the centre. The quiet 12...Re8 is the engine's first choice (about equal).
Why 12...f5 is the mistake: it threatens ...dxe4, but it leaves e5 and e6 weaker, and White just takes: 13.exf5 Bxf5 14.d4. The engine rates that more than a pawn better for White (about +1.1), clearly worse for Black than any of the quiet moves.
For White the take is the right one: 13.exf5 is the best by a margin (about +1.2). 13.exd5 Bxd5 is only a small edge (about +0.1), and 13.Nxe5 is a blunder that loses material.
Next time: when the opponent pushes a pawn to attack your pawn, first check whether you can simply take it before worrying about the threat.
